items.name: Product Hunt launch (self-hunt, free)
items.how_to_use: Log in with a personal account (company/brand accounts cannot post or comment) and click Submit -> New Product, enter your product URL, then schedule the launch up to 1 month ahead; posts go live at 12:01am PT because the homepage runs on a 24-hour Pacific cycle. Self-hunting is officially supported: 'posting yourself gives you full control over the launch' and no hunter is needed. Contribute a maker 'first comment' when you submit (70% of Product of the Day/Week/Month winners had one) introducing the team, key features, use cases and a request for feedback. Optionally create a free teaser up to 30 days ahead so interested people can opt into a notify-me email on launch day. Mechanism: web form; account must be a human personal account (Product Hunt requires community membership for at least a week before you gain access to contribute a product) — signup/aging cannot be safely automated.
items.rules_and_risks: Product Hunt is free for everyone. Promotion rule: you can share your launch link however you wish, but you cannot ask people directly to upvote — ask for feedback, comments and opinions instead; asking specifically for upvotes is against policy and PH may ask you to remove social posts. No paying or giving monetary compensation in exchange for upvotes (disqualification); makers found spamming audiences or paying for upvotes get the product removed and spammers are permanently removed. No gated giveaway contests tied to launch activity. Brand/company accounts are not allowed; authenticity is enforced.
items.why_it_works: A single high-authority page concentrates a daily cycle of early-adopter attention: competing on the homepage leaderboard gives a brand-new product a spike of qualified traffic, real user feedback, and an indexed profile page on a domain that ranks well for 'alternatives/product for X' queries.

items.name: Google Search Console: sitemap submission, URL inspection & Search generative-AI inclusion control
items.how_to_use: Create a Google account and verify site ownership once (DNS, HTML file or meta tag — account creation and verification must be done by a human). Submit sitemap.xml (or an RSS/Atom feed) in Search Console, or push it via the Search Console API (webmaster-tools v1 sitemaps submit, documented on the sitemap page). Use URL Inspection to request indexing of the first key URLs. Keep Settings > Search generative AI set to Include (the default; rolled out worldwide Aug 31, 2026) so the site can appear in AI Overviews, AI Mode and AI-in-Discover, then monitor the Generative AI performance report and expand pages sitting in positions 8-20.
items.rules_and_risks: A sitemap is only a hint — indexing is never guaranteed and pages must satisfy Google's indexing, spam and helpful-content policies; the official AI-optimization guide warns against scaled low-value AI content. Choosing Exclude forfeits AI-surface traffic. Robust noindex/robots.txt mistakes can hide the whole site. Google's guide also states llms.txt and structured data are not used to select AI citations, so don't build the strategy on them.
items.why_it_works: Google's documentation states AI features in Search are grounded in the Search index and that generative AI features can bring impressions and traffic; Search Console is the only official surface to verify indexing, measure those impressions and control inclusion. A tactics guide retrieved this run mirrors this as the day-one quick win (submit sitemap, inspect priority URLs).
how_searched: webfetch: Google Search Central sitemap, AI-optimization and generative-AI-control docs
websearch: Search generative AI control setting / free organic traffic guides

items.name: Google Merchant Center free listings (surfaces across Google)
items.how_to_use: Create a Merchant Center account at merchants.google.com, verify your online store URL, and upload product data with the required attributes (id, title, link, image_link, price, description, availability, plus condition/brand/GTIN/MPN, shipping and return-policy data as applicable). When you create a new Merchant Center account you are opted in to free listings by default; existing accounts can confirm status under Marketing -> Marketing methods -> 'Free listings' card (Admin access needed to change it). Partner-created accounts ingest data via the Merchant API. Mechanism: product feed / Merchant API; account creation requires human store-URL verification and is not autonomously automatable.
items.rules_and_risks: Must follow Google's policies for showing products free across Google; shipping settings (or the [shipping] attribute) and a return policy are required, including for a long list of countries (US, UK, CA, AU, DE, FR, JP etc.). Google explicitly says products 'aren't guaranteed to show across Google' — eligibility depends on data quality and matching. Listing quality rules apply (no promotional text in images, accurate price/GTIN matching). Free listings work for both online and local in-store products.
items.why_it_works: Free listings put your catalog into Google Search, Images, Lens, YouTube, Gemini, the Shopping tab and the products module on Business Profile — organic placements on the highest-intent commercial queries without paying per click, feeding discovery straight to your product pages.

items.name: Pinterest (visual search + pinning)
items.how_to_use: Create a free business account (manual signup; no automated account creation). Make boards + image/video Pins for each important site page; every Pin carries a clickable URL back to your site (limits: 2,000 boards, 200,000 Pins). Write keyword-rich titles/descriptions — Pinterest is a visual search engine. For automation: create an app at developers.pinterest.com, get Trial access (free, pins visible only to creator), then request Standard access with a screen recording of your OAuth flow to create public Pins via POST /v5/pins with pins:write scope.
items.rules_and_risks: Trial-access Pins are invisible to other users until Standard approval; developer guidelines ban incentivizing saves, storing API data, or sharing credentials; pin-flooding or repetitive content gets accounts limited. Account creation is manual only.
items.why_it_works: Pinterest hit 619M global monthly active users in Q4 2025 (+12% YoY) with 80B+ monthly searches; users arrive with commercial intent and Pins stay discoverable for months, unlike posts on most social networks.

items.name: HARO (Help a Reporter Out) — free journalist query email digests
items.how_to_use: Sign up free with your email at www.helpareporter.com (relaunched under Featured.com after acquiring HARO from Cision in April 2025; first emails went out April 22, 2025). You receive journalist queries by email — up to 3 editions per weekday (morning/afternoon/evening) — filtered to your categories; reply directly to the journalist's email with a specific, useful answer, your name, title and company before the stated deadline. Journalists also submit queries via the site ('Submit a Query'). Mechanism: email newsletter + direct email reply; account is an email signup that a human must control — automating pitch blasts would violate the anti-spam posture.
items.rules_and_risks: Free for journalists and sources, ad-supported, no subscription needed. HARO now detects AI-generated responses (per HARO's own blog) and bans abusive accounts extremely aggressively ('We Ban a HARO Account Every 23 Minutes' is a HARO blog post) — pitch only topics you are genuinely qualified on, write human-specific answers, and never spam irrelevant queries. Coverage is never guaranteed; you are competing with other sources on deadline. Owned/operated by Featured.com (also runs Connectively, which relaunched June 2026 while HARO continues).
items.why_it_works: Reporters on deadline actively need quotable experts, so a well-targeted reply converts into real editorial mentions, bylines and backlinks from news sites — earned media that both sends referral traffic and adds domain authority that AI search engines increasingly cite.

items.name: IndexNow: instant URL notifications to Bing, Naver, Seznam, Yandex & Yep
items.how_to_use: Generate a random 8-128 character hex key, host it as {key}.txt at the site root, then GET or POST (batches of up to 10,000 URLs) to api.indexnow.org/indexnow or any participant endpoint whenever you publish or update pages; the key stays on-site so engines can verify ownership. Wire the call into the CMS publish hook so it fires automatically. Optional: verify the property in Bing Webmaster Tools.
items.rules_and_risks: Only submit your own URLs that return HTTP 200; a 429 response means you are submitting too fast. Keep the key file at the advertised location or verification breaks. IndexNow accelerates discovery only — pages still must be indexable, canonical and policy-compliant, and there is no ranking guarantee.
items.why_it_works: IndexNow's documentation says participating engines are notified immediately of new, updated or deleted URLs instead of waiting for a crawl, and Bing's own get-started page describes the same key-file plus HTTP submission flow. For a brand-new site this cuts days or weeks of discovery latency across several engines at once.
how_searched: websearch: IndexNow official documentation
webfetch: indexnow.org pages and Bing IndexNow get-started

items.name: ChatGPT search visibility: Bing Webmaster Tools + allowing OAI-SearchBot
items.how_to_use: Verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools (it can import properties from Google Search Console), submit the XML sitemap (Bing's blog says submitted sitemaps are processed at least every 24 hours), enable IndexNow from the dashboard, and use URL Inspection to fix pages Bing has not indexed; Bing also documents a URL Submission API for programmatic pushes. Separately, add a 'User-agent: OAI-SearchBot / Allow: /' rule to robots.txt so OpenAI can surface the site in ChatGPT's search features (robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to apply).
items.rules_and_risks: OpenAI's official crawler docs state sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers (they may still appear as navigational links); blocking GPTBot only affects training, not search. Bing Webmaster account creation is a manual step. Keep key pages server-rendered, indexable and canonical — JS-only or noindex content cannot be retrieved by either system.
items.why_it_works: Bing's official blog states Bing powers AI and search experiences including ChatGPT, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo and Microsoft Start; OpenAI's official docs say OAI-SearchBot is used to surface websites in ChatGPT's search features and recommend allowing it. Maintaining both indexes gives a new site two independent paths into AI answers instead of one.
how_searched: websearch: ChatGPT search OAI-SearchBot Bing index Webmaster Tools
webfetch: Bing Webmaster URL Submission help page

items.name: YouTube (channel + free Data API)
items.how_to_use: Create a free Google account and channel (manual signup). Publish how-to/explainer videos targeting queries your audience searches; put your site link in descriptions and pinned comments. Automation: enable the YouTube Data API in Google Cloud Console — free default quota is 10,000 units/day with a separate 100-calls/day bucket for videos.insert (uploads) and search.list; authenticate via OAuth 2.0. Optimize titles/thumbnails for search intent; videos also rank inside Google Search.
items.rules_and_risks: A separate undocumented 'Video Uploads per day' quota has been reported to block uploads after ~7/day despite unit headroom (GitHub issue googleapis/google-api-python-client#2753, May 2026); raising quota requires a compliance audit. Buying views or engagement bait violates YouTube policies and gets channels terminated. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: YouTube reached 2.53-2.58B users in 2025-26 and is the world's 2nd most-visited website after Google; it functions as the second-largest search engine, giving durable, compounding traffic to new channels.

items.name: Reddit: niche subreddits where your users already gather
items.how_to_use: Pick one or two subreddits that match the target audience, read each subreddit's sidebar rules first, and answer questions with the full value in the comment itself, linking the article only when it directly completes the answer. Build genuine comment history before ever posting a link; prefer native summaries over bare URLs. Accounts must be created and used by a real person — automated account creation is not permitted.
items.rules_and_risks: Reddit's site-wide Rule 2 requires you to 'Participate authentically in communities where you have a personal interest, and do not spam or engage in disruptive behaviors (including content manipulation)'; the same page notes moderators enforce each community's own rules and admins can escalate from warnings to account suspension. reddit.com and the old self-promotion wiki returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches this run, so subreddit rules must be read manually in a browser. A tactics guide adds the practical rule: participate first, promote second, or you will get ignored or banned.
items.why_it_works: Subreddits are pre-selected audiences actively asking the questions your site answers; a distribution guide retrieved this run recommends posting to one engaged subreddit per article with the answer first and the link second. GEO research retrieved this run also shows Reddit threads are heavily cited by AI answer engines, so useful comments can keep earning visibility long after posting.
how_searched: webfetch: redditinc.com Reddit Rules policy page (body extracted from saved output)
websearch: community distribution tactics and AI-answer citation sources

items.name: Medium (free publishing + import tool with canonical links)
items.how_to_use: Create a free account (manual signup; no public publishing API exists). Go to Stories → 'Import a story', paste the URL of any page you own; Medium fetches it into a draft, auto-backdates it and adds a canonical link to your original site so you are not penalized for duplicate content. Add up to 5 tags, then publish. Republish your best-performing pages; get featured by relevant publications for extra distribution.
items.rules_and_risks: Only import content you have rights to; the Partner Program (paid) is optional — free publishing works. Overly promotional or low-quality content gets limited distribution; there is no API for automated posting. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: Medium drew ~95-106M monthly views in 2025 (top-500 site); Medium's own August 2025 report says readers are shown stories 15M times/day, and its June 2025 report notes LLMs referred 404k visits — real recommendation, search and AI-referral traffic for free.

items.name: Google News: Publisher Center setup + Google News sitemap
items.how_to_use: Sign in to publishercenter.google.com with a Google account, add the publication (basic info, headquarters location, contact details) and verify the website property URL; add a Google News sitemap and follow the 'Help Google News discover your web crawled content' checklist so stories are crawlable. Content must comply with the Google News content policies linked from the help center.
items.rules_and_risks: The Publisher Center overview states Google automatically considers all web content for inclusion in Google News so you do not need to apply, but eligibility requires meeting Google's overall requirements and News content policies — thin, syndicated-only or policy-violating content will not be picked up. Sign-in and property verification are manual, and Publisher Center is not a CMS for authoring content.
items.why_it_works: A verified publication plus a News sitemap puts stories onto Google News and other Google news surfaces — an interest-driven feed where a focused new site can appear next to established outlets rather than competing only on classic blue-link rankings.

items.name: TikTok (organic video reach, no follower base needed)
items.how_to_use: Create a free account (manual signup; TikTok's Content Posting API is application-gated for businesses, so organic posting via the free app is the free mechanism). Post short videos (15-60s) that answer niche questions; hook viewers in the first 1-3 seconds; use 3-5 niche hashtags and keyword-rich captions/on-screen text (TikTok SEO — the For You feed now behaves like a search engine); post consistently (1-4/day); put your site link in your bio.
items.rules_and_risks: Engagement bait, bought views/followers and mass-DMing violate Community Guidelines and cause shadowbans; business accounts get fewer trending sounds; each video is judged independently, so weak content flatlines. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: TikTok's recommendation system distributes to non-followers in test batches regardless of follower count (per TikTok's transparency documentation cited in algorithm guides); it has ~1.99B users, and H2-2025 benchmark data shows +25% reach growth and a 5.0% engagement rate — the highest among major platforms.

items.name: SourceBottle: free journalist call-outs and expert profiles
items.how_to_use: Sign up free as a source, filter call-outs by industry and deadline, and reply with a short answer (the retrieved pitching guide suggests roughly 60 words containing one specific number and one anecdote) plus your bio and link. Also build a free Expert Profile so journalists can find you inbound, and track where mentions appear so you can republish them as social proof.
items.rules_and_risks: Respond only to genuinely relevant queries before the stated deadline; paid promotion tiers are optional upgrades, not required for free source participation. Off-topic or exaggerated pitches waste the journalist's time and can get your profile ignored — credentials and quotes must be truthful.
items.why_it_works: The site matches query call-outs from named media outlets with expert sources at no cost, and one placed quote yields an authoritative third-party citation — news outlets are also among the sources most frequently cited by AI answer engines according to GEO research retrieved this run.

items.name: AI answer-engine visibility via robots.txt crawler allowlists
items.how_to_use: Edit your /robots.txt to explicitly allow PerplexityBot (Perplexity's crawler that surfaces and links websites in its search results), plus GPTBot, ClaudeBot and Applebot-Extended for ChatGPT/Claude/Apple answers. If behind Cloudflare or AWS WAF, create allow rules matching Perplexity's user agents AND the IP ranges it publishes at perplexity.com/perplexitybot.json (and perplexity-user.json). Verify with curl -A 'PerplexityBot' -I on a public page. Optionally add a small /llms.txt as a cheap hedge. No account needed; changes take effect within ~24 hours.
items.rules_and_risks: Perplexity-User (fetches triggered by a user's question) generally ignores robots.txt — only a firewall rule controls it, and blocking it makes your page unreadable in answers. Cloudflare documented Perplexity stealth crawlers evading blocks in Aug 2025, and some CDNs now challenge its UA, so check server logs. llms.txt is NOT a proven lever: Ahrefs found 97% of 137,000 llms.txt files received zero crawler requests (May 2026) and Google says it does not use the file — treat it as housekeeping, not a citation driver.
items.why_it_works: Perplexity officially recommends allowing PerplexityBot for inclusion in its search results, and AI answer engines increasingly send referral traffic; the whole tactic costs minutes and zero money, with no account or API required.
how_searched: PerplexityBot robots.txt allow Perplexity crawl your site
llms.txt standard website AI crawlers adoption

items.name: Threads API — official free cross-posting to Threads
items.how_to_use: Create a Meta developer app, connect a Threads account, obtain permissions threads_basic and threads_content_publish, then publish via the documented flow: POST the media/text container, then POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish; check quota with GET /{threads-user-id}/threads_publishing_limit. Official rate limits: calls within 24 hours = 4800 * number of impressions (impressions minimum defaults to 10), plus CPU-time caps, and profiles are limited to 250 API-published posts per rolling 24 hours (carousels count as one). Mechanism: official free Graph API; requires a human-owned Threads account and a Meta app — neither can be created autonomously (human identity/login verification), and app review is needed before exposing it publicly.
items.rules_and_risks: You may only publish on a person's behalf and display those posts to the person who created them within your app (per official overview) — no undisclosed ghost-posting for others. 250-post/day profile cap and impression-based call budgets mean bulk automation will hit limits; platform spam policies still apply to account-level behavior. API surface can change; enforce limits in your app as Meta instructs.
items.why_it_works: Threads is Meta's fast-growing text feed with real organic reach and no chronological-paywall problems: an official API lets a new site atomize blog posts into daily threads automatically, keeping a distribution channel warm with near-zero marginal effort — a rare case where posting automation is explicitly sanctioned by the platform.

items.name: SmartNews (free publisher distribution via SmartFormat RSS)
items.how_to_use: Prepare an RSS 2.0 or Atom feed of your editorial content; validate it against the SmartFormat Specification using SmartNews' feed validator (many existing feeds already validate; a WordPress plugin helps). Fill out the publisher application form at about.smartnews.com/en/press/publishers.html with your feed and full details; their team reviews applications and contacts you if your brand fits. Once accepted, articles appear in SmartNews US topic channels with links back to your site, rendered in their native SmartView reader. No account or API needed to apply.
items.rules_and_risks: Free but editorial: 'we review applications based on the current content needs of our product' and may never respond due to volume; the feed must validate as SmartFormat; US edition only; aimed at journalistic/editorial publications, not personal blogs or pure aggregators. Application is manual.
items.why_it_works: SmartNews partners with 300+ media companies and 3,000+ brands and distributes through its news app's topic channels, giving a new site free placement alongside major publishers with a native, fast reading experience.

items.name: Google Business Profile (free placement on Search + Maps)
items.how_to_use: Go to business.google.com/add and click 'Add your business to Google' (requires a Google Account, created manually). Enter business name, category, address or service area, website URL, hours and photos; verify the profile (postcard, phone, email or video depending on eligibility); then keep details current, post updates and respond to reviews. Free, no fees for any feature.
items.rules_and_risks: Only eligible real businesses (storefront or service area) qualify; fake listings, keyword-stuffed names or unverifiable businesses get removed; verification blocks edits until completed. Multi-location businesses must verify each location. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: Google states creating a Business Profile is free and it surfaces your business on Google Search and Maps — exactly where local-intent searches happen — with insights into which keywords people use to find you.

items.name: HackerNoon free story submission (human editor review)
items.how_to_use: Create an account, click 'Start Writing' / the Write button (top right), write or upload your story in the WYSIWYG editor, then Story Settings -> 'Submit Story for Review'. Required fields include a featured image, meta description, a TL;DR and up to 8 tags plus story indicators; you can leave a note to editors. Every story goes through an open editorial pool where any of the on-shift human editors can pick it up (editor shifts shown across UTC-7 to UTC+11). Mechanism: web editor submission; account signup needs a human email — not autonomously automatable (a bot mass-submitting would fail editorial review anyway).
items.rules_and_risks: Publishing is free with 'no pop-ups, no paywalls'; content goes through human editorial review and must follow HackerNoon's editorial guidelines (publishing philosophy, republishing rules, backlink rules, headlines, grammar, plagiarism checks). You keep ownership: 'you own your content and can remove it at anytime'. Stories must fit tech topics; expect rejection feedback rather than guaranteed publication. Features like automatic audio conversion and 12-language translations are applied by the platform to accepted stories.
items.why_it_works: HackerNoon claims 4,000,000+ monthly readers, 50,000+ published writers, an audience that is 64% aged 18-34 and 27% US, and top demographic 'technophiles' — so a genuinely useful technical article gets curated distribution on a high-authority tech domain plus syndication (audio/translations), driving referral traffic and credentialed backlinks without any ad spend.

items.name: Apple Business Connect — claim your location on Apple Maps
items.how_to_use: Sign up at businessconnect.apple.com (Apple Business) with a user whose role can manage locations -> Brands -> Locations -> Add -> enter the location name, address, primary category, status, phone and an optional website address (a Facebook, Instagram or TikTok page can be used instead of a website) -> set hours -> choose or create a brand -> verify the organization (first location is sent to Apple for review; if the location already exists on Maps you may verify with a phone call and a 4-digit code). The listing then shows logo, hours, images and key details on Apple Maps ('Claim your location on Maps so millions of customers can connect with your business'). Mechanism: web console; account + organization verification needs human interaction (mail from apple.com domains must be allowed) — not autonomously automatable.
items.rules_and_risks: Requires a real, verifiable location/address — this channel fits businesses with local presence, not anonymous websites. If the location is already claimed by another organization you must continue and request a transfer (review up to 5 business days with documentation). Photo and text standards apply to showcases/actions. Apple's guide (updated April 2026) shows no listing fee, but confirm current terms in-country. Feature availability varies by country and region.
items.why_it_works: Maps is a default discovery surface on every iPhone/Mac: a verified, optimized place card captures 'near me' and brand searches inside Apple Maps and Siri results — a distribution surface most competitors neglect, with a website link straight back to your domain.

items.name: Connectively (HARO's successor — new facts on the free plan)

Sign up for the free Starter plan (manual signup), build an expert profile with credentials, and answer up to 3 journalist queries per month; the free plan also includes early access to HARO queries, 1 monthly bylined-article submission, 1 monthly interview-profile submission, 3 keyword alerts and 10 monthly Find Journalists searches. items.name: Mastodon (fediverse, fully documented free API)
items.how_to_use: Create a free account on an instance matching your niche (many allow self-registration; some require admin approval — all manual, no automated account creation). Register an app on your instance to get an OAuth user token with write:statuses scope, then post via POST /api/v1/statuses (public/unlisted visibility, media, polls, scheduling). Engage in hashtag timelines and reply to others' posts; your posts can also federate to Mastodon users from other instances via ActivityPub.
items.rules_and_risks: Automated account creation is against instance rules and platform norms; link-only or mass posting gets you silenced/locked; bot accounts must be labeled; each instance sets its own ToS and can suspend you. Content is public by default on a federated network.
items.why_it_works: The API is completely free, open and documented — no approval process beyond OAuth — and the federated network gives new accounts organic discovery through hashtag timelines and shares, unlike follower-gated platforms.

items.name: Indie Hackers (founder community with built-in early-adopter audience)
items.how_to_use: Create a free account (manual signup). Write transparent posts about building/launching your site — traffic, revenue, failures, lessons — with a link to your site in the body; answer other founders' questions in comments; share progress updates. Case study on the site: a team went from 150 to 500 users with zero ad spend via IH posts, directory submissions and newsletter cross-promos. IH's own analysis of 450+ founders ranks community channels and Hacker News among the top first-user sources.
items.rules_and_risks: Overt self-promotion without genuine insight gets downvoted/removed; comment-spamming links violates community rules; one account per person; posts must be real stories, not ads. No public posting API.
items.why_it_works: The audience is exactly early adopters who click through to new products; documented founder case studies show free signups and users from well-written IH posts and community participation.

items.name: Original research, benchmarks and downloadable content upgrades
items.how_to_use: Publish one primary-source asset per quarter — a small-N benchmark or survey (the retrieved guide notes even N=20 comparisons win links because they are hard to copy) — and attach one downloadable content upgrade (checklist, template, spreadsheet) to each pillar page. Package findings as citable stats and pitch them with a 'scoop, source, support' note offering the underlying file.
items.rules_and_risks: Data must be real with methodology disclosed; fabricated numbers destroy trust. Follow Google's helpful-content and spam guidance in the official AI-optimization guide — it warns that scaled, low-value content production is a policy violation, so ship fewer, genuinely first-hand assets rather than mass-generated 'research'.
items.why_it_works: Comparison and benchmark formats earn links per hour invested because readers cannot get the numbers anywhere else; journalists, bloggers and AI answer engines all prefer citing concrete primary statistics over generic prose, so one dataset can keep producing citations and links over time.

items.name: Free instant web directories with no account: DevElif and Directory Index
items.how_to_use: On DevElif, either use the submission form or POST JSON to https://develif.com/api/submit with url, email, name, English description and category — no key, no login — and the listing publishes instantly with a public page, dofollow link, sitemap entry and JSON-LD structured data. Reuse one submission kit (URL, name, honest description, category) across a handful of quality free directories such as Directory Index, re-checking yearly for dead listings; handle larger launch platforms that require sign-up manually.
items.rules_and_risks: DevElif requires an English name/description, one listing per domain and no adult content; advertising on the site is paid but the listing itself stays free. Bulk-submitting to hundreds of low-quality directories is a waste and looks like link spam — favor a few relevant, live directories with real editorial standards, and keep descriptions honest.
items.why_it_works: An instant dofollow link plus structured data gives a brand-new domain its first crawlable, citable references, helping discovery systems find the site at all; curated directories also feed 'best X tools' style queries used by both search engines and AI answer engines.

items.name: Stack Exchange network (high-intent Q&A traffic)
items.how_to_use: Create a free account (manual signup) on the site matching your niche (Webmasters, Super User, Ask Ubuntu, Security, etc.). Write genuinely detailed answers to questions your audience asks; when you mention your own product/site, disclose affiliation in the post (e.g. 'disclosure: I'm the author'); link only to specific, directly relevant pages — never your homepage. Open-source projects and nonprofits can also apply for free community promotion ads. Note: the free Stack Exchange API is read-only, so answers must be written manually.
items.rules_and_risks: Overt self-promotion is voted down and flagged as spam; undisclosed affiliation violates the Acceptable Use Policy; link-only answers get deleted; a pattern of linking to your site gets you banned from the network.
items.why_it_works: Answers rank in Google and reach people with high-intent, search-driven questions in your exact topic; the network's promotion policy explicitly permits relevant, disclosed mentions, and free promo ads exist for OSS/nonprofits.

items.name: SaaSHub (free software directory with verification + alternatives traffic)
items.how_to_use: Search SaaSHub first — products are auto-aggregated from Product Hunt, GitHub and AppSumo, so your product may already be listed; if so, claim it via 'Verify' using either an email address on the product's domain or an HTML snippet added to your site (both free). If unlisted, submit through the submit form (requires a released product on its own domain, in English; agencies, waitlist landing pages and free-subdomain products are rejected). Then, from the management page, add yourself as an alternative on every competitor page you genuinely replace — that is where high-intent 'alternatives to X' traffic lives. Re-verify quarterly. Free account, manual signup.
items.rules_and_risks: All submissions go through an approval process and can be rejected or removed; featured placement is paid (skip it — basic listing is free); claiming competitor slots you don't actually replace risks removal. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: Free listing with a backlink and access to buying-intent search traffic; SaaSHub's free 'submit' tool also cross-posts to a monitored list of 110+ startup directories.
how_searched: SaaSHub add your product free listing claim

items.name: Podcast guesting and cross-promotion swaps with peer sites
items.how_to_use: Pitch small niche podcasts with a specific angle and one concrete number — the retrieved guide suggests shows under about 1,000 listeners and reports a single episode usually nets a show-notes dofollow link plus 10-30 referral visits. Reciprocate with peers of similar size: guest posts, newsletter shoutouts, joint webinars and content swaps, each linking to a genuinely useful resource on your site (checklist or hub page).
items.rules_and_risks: Never buy links or run pay-for-placement schemes; keep collaborations strictly on-topic so the audiences overlap, disclose sponsorship relationships, and don't scale pitches with automated mail merges — irrelevant or mass pitches get ignored and damage reputation.
items.why_it_works: Borrowed audiences convert far better than cold traffic: a guest post or episode puts the site in front of listeners who already trust the host, and the retrieved guides note guest posts and newsletter/podcast/webinar collaborations produce backlinks plus referral visitors while compounding as both audiences overlap.

items.name: There's An AI For That (TAAFT) — AI tool directory
items.how_to_use: For AI tools only: sign in free (manual signup) and submit via the launch form with name, URL, tagline, description and logo; all submissions are manually reviewed by staff. Free listings also happen through a monthly X thread where indie makers submit and one tool is listed free each month. Once listed, updates are free and self-service for verified tools, and listings don't expire — newer tools rank higher, so traffic compounds while the listing lives.
items.rules_and_risks: Submissions are manually reviewed and can be rejected under editorial policy; a paid 'Get Featured' option ($437 one-off) exists — don't buy it for reach; free submissions are limited (monthly thread model) so approval can take time; only AI tools, GPTs and AI influencers are accepted.
items.why_it_works: TAAFT is one of the largest AI-tool discovery directories with high-intent search traffic; free, permanent listings give long-tail exposure, and the directory explicitly offers free submission paths.

items.name: Podcast Index (free, open podcast directory with free API)
items.how_to_use: If you have a podcast (or start one about your topic): sign up for a free API key at api.podcastindex.org (manual signup), then register your feed via GET /api/1.0/add/byfeedurl?url=YOUR_FEED — this endpoint requires a read-write key. Your show becomes searchable in this free, open, nonprofit directory and in apps that consume it; publish episodes whose show notes link back to your site. Requests must include a descriptive User-Agent header and a signed Authorization header (SHA-1 of key+secret+unix time).
items.rules_and_risks: The API requires request signing and self-identification; the feed must be a valid RSS podcast feed; the directory is donation-funded with no paid placement; spam feeds are removed. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: It is a genuinely free, open, nonprofit directory with a documented free API for adding podcasts by feed URL — no company gatekeeping — complementing Apple/Spotify listings and driving referral traffic through show notes.

items.name: Eventbrite free events (free event pages that rank in search)
items.how_to_use: Create a free organizer account (manual signup). Publish an event with a 'Free' ticket type (optional capacity limit); write a keyword-rich description and add your website link; publish. Since September 4, 2024, Eventbrite is free to publish unlimited events of any size, and free tickets carry no service or processing fees for you or attendees. Promote the event page; attendees land on your Eventbrite page and click through to your site.
items.rules_and_risks: Paid tickets incur a 3.7% + $1.79 service fee (paid by attendee by default); fake or misleading events get removed; Eventbrite Ads are paid add-ons — skip them to stay free. Account creation is manual.
items.why_it_works: Eventbrite event pages rank in Google and its own events marketplace; free workshops, webinars and meetups attract real people who click through to your site, at zero cost for free events.

items.name: AlternativeTo 'Suggest new application' listing
items.how_to_use: Create a free AlternativeTo account (email verification is mandatory before you can submit — the site does this 'to discourage spammers and bots'), then use User icon (top right) -> 'Suggest new application' -> fill Platforms, License, Description, Tags -> 'Submit the application'. You can also add your product as an alternative to a competitor via the competitor's page -> 'Contribute to this page' -> 'Suggest Alternatives'. Optional one-time $5 priority review moves you to the front of the queue (usually reviewed within 1-2 business days, up to a week in busy periods); paying does not buy approval. Mechanism: web form; account creation needs human email verification — not autonomously automatable.
items.rules_and_risks: Free to submit; the normal queue holds several thousand apps with no promised review date, and your app is invisible to everyone until approved (and gone entirely if declined). Strict criteria: English-language software only; nothing unreleased/closed-beta/invite-only; no hardware; no content sites (blogs, newspapers, review/comparison/coupon sites); one-off calculator/converter/PDF/QR-style tools are declined; thin LLM wrappers, AI companion/headshot tools and 'directories of AI tools' are declined; no links, phone numbers or emails inside descriptions; UTM parameters on the Official Website link are rejected; using your user profile to advertise is blocked as spam; incentivized upvotes or fake accounts can drop your rank or remove you from the front page.
items.why_it_works: AlternativeTo ranks on high-intent 'alternatives to X' queries, so a verified listing intercepts users actively shopping for competitors — one of the few directories where traffic arrives with purchase/switch intent rather than casual browsing.

items.name: daily.dev (Squads + Direct Posting + source feeds)
items.how_to_use: Register free, then pick a path: (1) create a public Squad and post your own articles/links there; (2) 'Suggest new source' with your publication's public RSS/Atom feed (Sources section -> enter feed URL -> Check link -> Submit for review); (3) click 'New Post' anywhere to directly post a link to your own page. Add twitter:creator meta to articles and claim ownership to get analytics. There is a documented public GraphQL API (and MCP server) for reading feeds; writing posts is done in the app UI.
items.rules_and_risks: Sources must be well-known publications or developer blogging platforms; corporate and personal blogs are explicitly excluded, manual review up to 30 days, and only content published AFTER approval is indexed. Squads and direct posts must follow content guidelines; low-quality/self-promotional spam gets removed and can cost your account. Account cannot be auto-created.
items.why_it_works: Reaches a large developer audience through an algorithmic new-tab extension feed plus a public sources directory; official docs describe three legit on-ramps including automatic RSS indexing for qualifying publications.

items.name: Hacker News: Show HN and story submissions

items.rules_and_risks: HN's official guidelines state the site must not be used primarily for promotion, forbid generated or automated posts and automated account activity, require original titles and forbid deleting and reposting to refresh a story, restrict submissions to on-topic tech/computer matters, and prohibit soliciting votes. items.name: Dev.to (Forem) cross-publishing via the official Forem API

items.rules_and_risks: Always set canonical_url to the original article — the API docs describe it as the way to maintain SEO integrity for cross-posts; duplicate copies without canonicals split ranking signals. The account and API key must be created manually, and platform moderation/tag rules still apply to what you publish.
items.why_it_works: The official Forem API makes cross-posting free and programmable (one authenticated POST per article), and dev.to's topic feeds put content in front of an existing developer readership without needing your own audience yet.

items.name: Substack Notes as a growth engine
items.how_to_use: Publish on Substack (free) and post in Notes — short-form posts, links, quotes, images and restacks that surface you in the Substack app's feeds before readers ever land on your newsletter; engage genuinely with others' notes and restack what you value. In an interview with Linda Lebrun from Substack's Writer Partnerships team (Feb 2025) she says she now starts writer conversations 'with Notes and with the app' rather than recommendations, and calls Notes where growth happens ('growth happens where engagement happens'). Mechanism: in-app social feed; requires a Substack account/publication (human email signup) — not autonomously automatable, and spammy growth tactics work against you.
items.rules_and_risks: No fixed posting quota — consistency and enjoyment matter more than volume ('short and sweet is king'). Avoid treating it like a LinkedIn/X growth hack or playing subscribe-for-subscribe games; the interviewed writer explicitly frames organic engagement, not gaming, as the source of results. Figures cited are one writer's self-reported outcome (about 25% of her ~11,000 subscribers attributed to Notes/app), not a platform guarantee. Results vary with niche and effort.
items.why_it_works: Notes is inside Substack's own network effects: the app is a top-download product where restacks and comments put a new publication in front of readers who are already in buying/reading mode for newsletters, converting app engagement into subscriptions without needing an existing audience — a cold-start solution for brand-new sites.

items.name: Flipboard (RSS feed -> auto magazines in topic feeds)

items.why_it_works: Flipboard distributes flipped articles into topic feeds with hundreds of thousands to millions of readers based on subject, and links open the original source (traffic lands on your site), giving a new blog passive discovery without an existing follower base.

items.name: Bluesky starter packs + custom feeds for your niche
items.how_to_use: Create a Bluesky account, then from your profile's Starter Packs tab build a pack (use 'Make one for me' to auto-generate or 'Create' to hand-pick) recommending up to 150 people and up to 3 custom feeds — include your own site's account among them — and share the pack link/QR code on your site and other networks; new users who join via your pack get your recommended follows and feeds, and you get notified when they join. Custom feeds let you (or anyone) set any algorithm/topic as a home timeline — examples shown are Quiet Posters, Science and Catch Up. Anyone with a Bluesky account can do this. Mechanism: in-app feature; account creation is a human mobile/email flow — not autonomously automatable.

Packs are moderation-governed: users can block the creator to drop out of a pack, and packs can be reported to Bluesky's moderation team under the Community Guidelines. Don't add people who don't want to be there; no fake-account seeding (platform-managed, and duplicate/automated accounts violate Bluesky norms).
items.why_it_works: Starter packs are an official onboarding primitive: every new user who joins through your pack adopts your niche's accounts and feeds — meaning you shape what a cohort of fresh users sees, compounding your account's reach inside an engagement-driven, chronological-ish network that early adopters and tech audiences use heavily.

items.name: Telegram channel + official Bot API

items.why_it_works: Telegram has a very large global user base, channels are indexed in Telegram search, and the Bot API is a documented free HTTP interface, so publishing is automatable once you own a channel.

items.name: Web Stories in Google Search and Discover

items.name: Kagi Small Web inclusion (GitHub list of personal-blog feeds)
items.how_to_use: Add your site's RSS/Atom feed to smallweb.txt in the kagisearch/smallweb repo (one-click 'Add website RSS feed' edit link opens the file) and submit a pull request. No Kagi account is required — only a GitHub account for the PR route (email/issue routes aren't offered here; GitHub sign-up is a human step). Feed shows in Kagi search results, and on kagi.com/smallweb if the blog has posts under 7 days old and can render in an iframe.

YouTube channels: under 100k subscribers and at most 2 videos/week. Removal requests are honored when guidelines break. So this works only for authentic personal-blog-style sites — a commercial content farm will be rejected.
items.why_it_works: Kagi surfaces Small Web posts directly in its search results (1.7k-star repo, feeds also exposed via Kagi's RSS feed and OPML), giving personal writing distribution inside a search engine built to reward human, non-LLM content — exactly the anti-AI-slop positioning that is scarce in 2026.

items.name: Qiita API v2 — publish developer articles programmatically

Articles must be genuinely useful technical write-ups; duplicated/syndicated content and promotional posts erode standing. The API is free but tokens carry your account's identity — never expose the token (it grants read_qiita/write_qiita on your account).
items.why_it_works: Qiita is a high-traffic developer article platform where well-tagged tutorials surface in site search and Google for programming questions; having an official API means one integration lets you keep a technical blog mirrored to a developer audience that actively searches for how-to content.

items.name: Marginalia Search — independent-web index submission
items.how_to_use: Four official routes per the repo README: (A) search 'site:yoursite.com' on Marginalia's search page — if the domain is already known, a button appears to add it manually; (B) fork the submit-site-to-marginalia-search repo, add your URL to sites.txt, open a PR (applied when the next crawl runs, 'a month or more — be patient'); (B1/2) open a GitHub issue with your URL; (C) email the URL to contact@marginalia-search.com (no reply expected). Separately, for 'random exploration' discovery, use the 'suggest' button under your site's screenshot. Only route C needs no account at all; GitHub routes need a GitHub account (human signup).
items.rules_and_risks: Manual submission is deliberate anti-abuse friction — 'Adding obstacles makes this much harder. Otherwise it would be possible to use the search engine's crawler essentially as a weapon'. Expect slow inclusion (a month+ until crawl cycle) and no email confirmation. Marginalia is tiny versus Google, so treat it as incremental indie-web discovery and link equity from a genuinely independent index, not a traffic flood. Don't mass-submit hundreds of URLs — that's exactly what the friction is designed against.
items.why_it_works: Marginalia indexes the small/indie web that commercial engines under-crawl; inclusion gets your pages into a crawler that actively promotes independent sites, earning you visibility (and a backlink-adjacent presence) among readers deliberately seeking non-corporate content.

items.name: Brave Search URL submission
items.how_to_use: Open the public Submit URL page and submit your canonical pages (homepage, key category/content pages); no account needed. Ensure robots.txt allows Bravebot and that pages are crawlable by Googlebot (Brave gates crawling on Googlebot-crawlability), then monitor manually.
items.rules_and_risks: Submission is a discovery/re-fetch request, not a guarantee of indexing; there is no Brave webmaster console, sitemap ingestion, or API, and Brave ignores robots.txt for de-indexing (use noindex). Spammy/low-quality pages still won't surface.
items.why_it_works: Brave runs its own independent index and its search results feed Claude's web search, so being indexed in Brave is a cheap route to visibility in an AI answer engine as well as Brave/AI-browser users.

items.name: Wiby submit — indie search engine for simple web pages
items.how_to_use: Open wiby.me/submit/, enter your page URL, choose the worksafe flag, solve the image CAPTCHA (cookies must be enabled) and submit — no account, no email, no API key required. Official indexing guidance: 'Pages must be simple in design. Simple HTML, non-commercial sites are preferred. Pages should not use much scripts/css for cosmetic effect.'
items.rules_and_risks: Designed against the modern ad-heavy web: no intrusive ads (ads over content), don't use Wiby as 'a portal to other bloated websites', avoid submitting many pages from one site ('In most cases, only the page you submit will be crawled'), pages with no text or using frames need a meta description tag, Angelfire/Tripod pages are no longer grandfathered because their ads are too intrusive. The CAPTCHA inherently blocks automated submission, and heavy commercial or script-laden sites simply won't be indexed — this channel only fits lean, non-commercial pages.
items.why_it_works: Wiby deliberately surfaces lightweight, independent pages that Google buries under ad-heavy results; its users are exactly the small-web audience that tends to link, bookmark and community-share indie sites, so inclusion delivers qualified, culture-aligned discovery even at modest volume.

items.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata presence (tactic)
items.how_to_use: Only pursue this once you have independent coverage. Gather significant coverage in reliable, independent sources about your subject, ensure (or find) a Wikipedia article under the General Notability Guideline, and add accurate, cited facts with a neutral tone. Add/complete the matching Wikidata item; Wikidata/Wikipedia feed knowledge panels and AI answers and pass strong authority signals.
items.rules_and_risks: Self-promotion is against Wikipedia policy; editing about yourself/your company triggers conflict-of-interest rules and articles lacking independent sources are deleted. Notability requires multiple independent reliable sources (not your own site/press releases). Wikipedia accounts/bots cannot be auto-created; undisclosed paid/direct editing gets banned.
items.why_it_works: Wikipedia and Wikidata are among the most-cited surfaces by search engines and AI assistants, so a genuinely sourced entry produces durable, high-authority referral and citation effects — but only for topics that legitimately meet notability.
